author: Sample commentary (synthetic data)
headline: 13 measures were dropped and targets were made easier 247 times, 134 of them right after a miss.
paragraphs: Measures disappear for good reasons (a program ends, a better measure replaces it) and for convenient ones. The list shows each dropped measure, its last value and whether it was being met. A target that becomes easier the year after a miss is the clearest signal of target-chasing; it is not misconduct, but it changes what the 'met' share means.
Read with the outcomes view: a department with a high met share and many lowered targets is different from one with a high met share and stable targets.

templates.template: {depts_fmt} departments, FY{fy0}–FY{fy1}: {dropped_fmt} measures dropped ({dropped_missed_fmt} were being missed when dropped); targets made easier {lowered_fmt} times, {lowered_after_miss_fmt} the year after a miss.
templates.fallback: Too few records match to summarize; widen the years or clear a filter.

caveats.text: A renamed measure looks like a drop plus an addition; the pipeline matches names with a similarity threshold and lists uncertain matches.
